# PaperTrail Agent API

> Public research-paper metadata and citation relationships, with a static HTTPS API, query SDKs, SQLite database and local MCP tools. No API key required.

- [Agent guide](https://jimmywuhkust.github.io/papertrail/agents/): human-readable instructions and working query examples.
- [Complete plain-text guide](https://jimmywuhkust.github.io/papertrail/agents/README.md): transport, parameters, SQL schema, MCP configuration and evidence limitations.
- [API manifest](https://jimmywuhkust.github.io/papertrail/api/v1/manifest.json): source snapshot, exact coverage, database download, checksums and search shard URLs.
- [OpenAPI](https://jimmywuhkust.github.io/papertrail/api/v1/openapi.json): actual static HTTPS GET endpoints.
- [MCP tool schemas](https://jimmywuhkust.github.io/papertrail/api/v1/tools.json): six query tools, run using the local Python MCP stdio server.
- [Python SDK and MCP server](https://jimmywuhkust.github.io/papertrail/agents/papertrail.py): Python 3.11+, no dependencies; verified download and local cache; search, paper, references, cited_by, related, graph.
- [JavaScript SDK](https://jimmywuhkust.github.io/papertrail/agents/papertrail.mjs): Node.js 22+ or browser; lightweight venue searches, paper lookup, references, citedBy and text similarity.

## Agent workflow

1. Read the manifest and record the snapshot timestamp. Metadata covers 2016–2025 in ten venues, not the worldwide live literature.
2. Use Python search(q, venue=..., limit=...) or JavaScript search(q, {venue: ...}). Get a stable id or resolve a DOI/OpenAlex id with paper().
3. Get references()/cited_by() for recorded citation edges; related(method="coupling"|"cocitation"|"text") for inferred similarity; graph() for bounded citation neighborhoods.
4. Cite the original paper/sourceUrl. Distinguish snapshot incoming edges from upstream global citationCount. External identifier nodes lack metadata; empty references can mean missing data.

GitHub Pages serves static resources. Appending ?q=... does not execute a query, and there is no hosted POST or HTTP MCP endpoint. Execute queries with the downloaded SDK, local SQLite or local MCP stdio tools. First Python query downloads a ~157 MB compressed database and caches a ~479 MB verified SQLite file. For lighter requests use the JavaScript SDK with a venue filter.
